h1: The 7 Best Under-Desk Keyboard Tray Drawers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Under-Desk Keyboard Trays: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven under-desk keyboard trays and drawers compared on width, clamp or screw mounting, height adjustment and mouse space.
summary: The Mount-It! tray with an adjustable mouse platform is our top pick because it combines height adjustment, a smooth slide and a separate mouse surface. The Kensington is the widest option at 24.5 inches, the Fellowes is the three-position drawer for standard keyboards, and the VIVO 27 by 11 clamp-on is the value pick.
intro: The measurement that ruins most keyboard tray purchases is not the tray, it is the desk. A tray hangs from the underside, so the thickness of the desktop, any front lip, a curved edge or a drawer rail can stop it from mounting. Several listings here warn about exactly this, with one stating that it needs at least 31.3 inches of width and 11.8 inches of depth.

We ranked seven trays on what you can verify from a listing: tray width and depth, whether it clamps or screws on, how many height or tilt positions it offers, and whether the mouse has somewhere to go. We reviewed specifications, not desks, so treat the dimensions as the starting point and measure your own clearance underneath before you order.

products.name: Mount-It! Keyboard Tray Under Desk with Adjustable Mouse Platform, Easy-Glide
products.verdict: A height-adjustable shelf with a smooth sliding mechanism and a movable mouse platform.
products.description:
The Mount-It! tray is an under-desk keyboard shelf with a smooth sliding mechanism, height adjustment and an adjustable mouse platform. Height adjustment is the key detail, because a tray at the wrong height forces your wrists to bend upward.

It earns the top slot by pairing a stated glide, adjustable height and a separate mouse surface in a single tray. The Kensington is wider, but its listing mentions a wrist rest rather than a movable mouse area, and the VIVO trays rely on tilt angles.

Best for a daily typist who wants the keyboard tucked away. The caveat is the $50 to $100 bucket, which costs more than clamp-on rivals.
products.idealFor: Daily typists who want an adjustable keyboard and mouse shelf.
products.skipIf: You only need the cheapest clamp-on tray.

products.name: Kensington Keyboard Tray Under Desk
products.verdict: An extra-wide 24.5 inch tray that fits oversize and ergonomic keyboards plus a wrist rest.
products.description:
Kensington's tray is extra wide at 24.5 inches, and the listing says it fits all keyboard sizes, including oversize and ergonomically shaped models, with room for a wrist rest. Wide trays matter for split or curved ergonomic keyboards that standard shelves crowd.

It ranks second because its width is the group's best-documented fit for big keyboards, while the Mount-It adds a movable mouse platform. It beats the Fellowes on size because that tray is rated for keyboards up to 20 inches.

Suits a typist with an ergonomic keyboard and a wrist rest. The caveat is that a wide tray needs a wide desk, and the listing summary does not detail the mouse area.
products.idealFor: Typists using large or ergonomic keyboards.
products.skipIf: Your desk is narrow or you want a movable mouse tray.

products.name: Fellowes Office Suites Underdesk Keyboard Drawer
products.verdict: A true drawer with three height adjustments for standard keyboards up to 20 inches.
products.description:
The Fellowes is a drawer-style tray with three height adjustments, and its platform is spacious enough for keyboards up to 20 inches wide. The impact-resistant tray is meant for standard keyboards.

It ranks third because three preset heights are less flexible than the Mount-It's adjustment, and the 20 inch limit rules out wide ergonomic keyboards that suit the Kensington. It still beats the plain clamp-on trays by being a drawer, which gives a more finished look.

Good for an office desk with a standard keyboard. The caveat is the preset positions, so if none of the three matches your elbow height, you cannot fine-tune.
products.skipIf: You use a wide ergonomic keyboard.

products.name: VIVO Black Clamp-on 27 x 11 in Keyboard Tray
products.verdict: A 27 by 11 inch tray held by sturdy C-clamps, with adjustable typing angles.
products.description:
VIVO's 27 by 11 inch tray clamps to the desk with sturdy C-clamps and offers comfortable typing angles while saving desk space. The clamp mount avoids drilling, which suits rentals and shared desks.

It ranks fourth because the size is generous for a keyboard and mouse together, but its listing gives no height-adjust range like the Fellowes. It sits above the screw-mounted VIVO 25 by 10 because the clamp installs faster and the tray is bigger.

A smart buy for a desk where you do not want holes. The caveat is clamp clearance, since a thick desktop or front lip can prevent a C-clamp from gripping.
products.idealFor: Rentals and shared desks where drilling is off limits.
products.skipIf: Your desk edge is thick or has a lip.

products.name: VIVO Black Extra Large Clamp-on 34 x 11 in Keyboard Tray
products.verdict: A 34 by 11 inch extra-long clamp-on tray that holds a keyboard and mouse side by side.
products.description:
This VIVO is the longest tray in the ranking at 34 by 11 inches, and it clamps on with sturdy C-clamps and offers comfortable typing angles. The length leaves room for a full keyboard, a number pad and a mouse area.

It ranks fifth because a 34 inch tray needs a wide desk, and the $50 to $100 bucket is higher than the 27 inch VIVO that suits most users. It wins on raw space, since no other tray here matches it.

Works for a wide desk and a maker who wants room for a keyboard and a graphics tablet. The caveat is weight and leverage, so use well-seated clamps and keep heavy items off the far end.
cons: Costs more than the 27 inch model
products.idealFor: Wide desks needing room for a full workspace.
products.skipIf: Your desk is under 36 inches wide.

products.name: VIVO Black Under Desk 25 x 10 in Keyboard Tray
products.verdict: A deluxe 25 by 10 inch tray with ergonomic keyboard and mouse space and notes for height-adjustable desks.
products.description:
VIVO's 25 by 10 inch tray is described as a deluxe universal ergonomic keyboard and mouse tray, and the listing covers installing it on a height-adjustable desk. Mounting directions for sit-stand desks matter because the frame can interfere with a tray.

It ranks sixth because it is smaller than the clamp-on VIVO trays and lands in a higher bucket, $50 to $100, without a stated height range. It stays on the list because of its documentation for sit-stand desks.

A reasonable pick for a sit-stand desk where compatibility matters. The caveat is depth: 10 inches is tight for a keyboard plus a mouse.
products.idealFor: Sit-stand desks where compatibility is a concern.
products.skipIf: You need room for a mouse beside the keyboard.

products.name: BONTEC Under Desk Keyboard Tray
products.verdict: Frees monitor space and states its limits plainly: 31.3 inches of width and 11.8 inches of depth.
products.description:
BONTEC puts its limits up front. The tray will not work with desks that have curved edges, and it needs at least 31.3 inches of width and 11.8 inches of depth. It aims to move the keyboard and mouse below the desktop to free valuable space for monitors.

It ranks last because the strict requirements exclude more desks than the VIVO clamp-ons, and the listing says little about adjustment. It deserves credit for honesty, since that clarity prevents returns.

Best for a standard rectangular desk with clearance underneath. The caveat is the curved-desk exclusion, so it will not suit corner or L-shaped tops.
products.idealFor: Rectangular desks with enough clearance beneath.
products.skipIf: You have a curved, corner or L-shaped desk.

whatMatters.detail: A tray hangs below the desktop, so the thickness of the top, any front lip and drawer rails decide whether it fits. Check the gap between the top surface and your thighs, and compare it with the tray's stated depth. Clamps also need a flat edge to grip, which curved desks do not provide.

Width decides whether the mouse sits beside the keyboard, and depth decides your wrist angle. Trays of 25 inches suit compact keyboards, while 34 inches suit a full layout plus a mouse. Compare the stated numbers with your keyboard width and add roughly six inches for a mouse.

Elbows should sit near a right angle, so a tray at the wrong height forces your wrists to bend. Some trays offer presets, such as three positions, while others adjust continuously. Look for a stated range, and plan to sit at your normal height before judging.

Clamps install without drilling and move easily between desks, but they need clearance and can loosen under load. Screws are more secure but leave holes. Check which method the listing uses, and test the grip regularly if the tray is a clamp style.

A mouse at desk height while the keyboard is below forces an awkward reach. A tray with a mouse platform or enough width keeps both at one level. Look for a stated mouse area, and avoid trays that only mention the keyboard if you use a mouse all day.

faq.q: Will a keyboard tray fit my desk?
faq.a: Measure the width, the front-to-back depth and the thickness of the desktop edge. The BONTEC needs at least 31.3 inches by 11.8 inches, while clamp-on VIVO trays need a flat edge to grip.

faq.q: What mistake do people make with keyboard trays?
faq.a: Ignoring leg room. A tray that hangs too low hits the thighs, and one that hangs too high raises the wrists. Sit at your normal height with the Fellowes or Mount-It adjustment before locking it.

faq.q: Is the Mount-It worth more than the VIVO 27 by 11?
faq.a: For daily typists, yes, because the Mount-It adds height adjustment, a smooth glide and a movable mouse platform. The VIVO is a better value for occasional use or a rental desk.

faq.q: How do I install a clamp-on tray?
faq.a: Position the brackets so the tray sits level, tighten the C-clamps evenly, then test it by pushing down on the front edge. Retighten after a day, since clamps can settle on a thick desktop.

faq.q: How do I maintain a sliding tray?
faq.a: Wipe the runners with a dry cloth, check the screws or clamps monthly, and avoid resting heavy loads on the front edge. A drop of light lubricant on the Mount-It slide helps if it gets noisy.

faq.q: Can I use a tray on a curved or L-shaped desk?
faq.a: Often not. The BONTEC warns that it will not work with curved desks, and clamps need a flat edge. Look for a model with screw-in mounting and measure the straight section where the tray would go.

finalTake: The Mount-It! is the best under-desk keyboard tray here because it combines height adjustment, a smooth slide and a mouse platform. The Kensington is the one to buy for an ergonomic keyboard, and the VIVO 27 by 11 is the budget clamp-on. Measure your desk edge before you order, because fit decides everything.
